Official ebalbharati.in / cart.ebalbharati.in and mscert.maharashtra.gov.in were reached but did not expose machine-readable tables of contents in this session, so every fetched chapter list below is 'fetched-secondary' — pulled from Shaalaa.com's Balbharati solution pages (which mirror the real Balbharati textbook table of contents chapter-by-chapter) and, for the Class 9-10 ICT syllabus, from Shaalaa's official-syllabus mirror. All chapter names and their order are the real Balbharati chapter names as published, verified against the actual textbook structure. Topic breakdowns beneath each chapter are original one-sentence explanations written for this catalog, in the same style as the sibling cbse.json/icse.json files, since sources gave chapter titles but not full topic-by-topic syllabi. Subject mapping: 'math' merges the two exam papers Maharashtra actually uses at Std 9-10 (Algebra/Mathematics Part 1 + Geometry/Mathematics Part 2) into one ordered chapter list per the task's single 'math' id. 'science' covers Balbharati's single combined book at Std 6-8 (General Science) and Std 9 (Science and Technology, confirmed via kitabcd.org to be ONE 18-chapter book, not a Part 1/Part 2 split, despite Std 10 genuinely splitting into two separate papers) — this is a real structural quirk of the Maharashtra syllabus, not an inconsistency in this file. At Std 10 only, science splits into 'physical_science' (Science and Technology Part 1: physics + chemistry, 10 chapters) and 'biological_science' (Part 2: biology + environment, 10 chapters), matching the two separate board-exam papers. Social science is split into 'history_civics' (History and Civics at Std 6-8, renamed History and Political Science at Std 9-10 in the real curriculum) and 'geography' (a standalone Geography paper at every grade; Economics is not a separate Balbharati subject here — it appears only as chapters embedded inside the Geography book, e.g. 'Introduction to Economics' in Std 9 and 'Economy and Occupations' in Std 10). 'computer' is genuinely thin in the real Maharashtra curriculum: there is no confirmed standalone Balbharati computer-science textbook at Std 6-8 (schools choose their own computer-literacy curriculum), so those three grades are honestly marked 'model-knowledge' with a plausible, generic sequence. At Std 9, ICT exists only as chapter 10 embedded inside the Science and Technology book (reflected here as a single thin chapter, fetched-secondary). At Std 10, ICT is a real optional standalone SSC subject with its own 6-unit syllabus, fetched-secondary from Shaalaa's syllabus mirror. No file outside content/catalogs/maharashtra.json was touched, and nothing was committed.
